story.head: Stay out of the box, Kraken
paras: The Stars (15-8-2) lost 5-3 to St. Louis on Friday, while the Kraken (12-10-1) beat Edmonton 4-2 the same night. Going in, the Stars are fourth in the Central (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Kraken fourth in the Pacific (tied for 22nd).
The Stars’ record (.640) is about what their chances are worth. The Kraken’s record (.543) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.442), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Stars play slow, tight games (lowest) and have the league’s best penalty kill (1st). They also block more shots than anyone (1st), and the Kraken’s knack for getting shots through meets their shot blockers. Dallas has allowed 2.48 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. As for the Kraken, they rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd), give up a lot of shots (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). The Stars’ power play (1st) could do real damage against the Kraken’s penalty kill (30th).

Jason Robertson (12 G / 17 A / 29 P in 25 GP) is tied for the Stars’ scoring lead, with seven points in his last five games. Mikko Rantanen (10 G / 19 A / 29 P in 25 GP) shares it, with seven points in his last five games. For the Kraken, Berkly Catton (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Kaapo Kakko (6 G / 11 A / 17 P in 23 GP) is next in line.

Jake Oettinger (13-5-1 / .912 SV% in 19 GS) has been outstanding for Dallas and will likely start. Joey Daccord (6-5-0 / .881 SV% in 11 GS) is in line to start for Seattle. Daccord has a .869 save percentage in five starts against the Stars, well under his usual .906. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
The Stars usually control more of the chances than the Kraken do.
